observation: Front view (along the slit): one tube standing on the exposed drum top, centred in the slit, its root spreading into the floor through a smooth cove, its open muzzle near the top of the slit; the drum wall below the slit is unbroken and its rotation-ring seam runs straight across without a notch. Top view: the slit is a clean parallel-walled channel, the tube lies on its mid-line with clear air either side, the cove flare stops short of both walls, and the bore is open and round. Iso view: hemisphere on a visible drum on a bare square plate, the slit running from its far edge over the apex and down the near flank to the drum top, with only a short mouth clearing the shell. No arms, keel, pier or foot block anywhere; no floating, misplaced, missing or extra geometry, no visible intersection, no raw sawn face.
